title: Chromium: overrideable OAuth env and CVE security-floor upgrade
head: d5a888589b96
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: Localized pacman output prevents the security-floor upgrade
leads.consequence: With an installed vulnerable Chromium and a new enough repo build, pacman -Si under e.g. es_ES reports Versión rather than Version. The awk extracts nothing; the helper says no chromium package is available and exits 1. omarchy-migrate leaves this and all later migrations pending, omarchy update stops before post-update hooks/AUR, and every retry under that locale repeats the failure. Use a locale-stable query or LC_ALL=C on the pacman invocation.

leads.summary: A flags-file read error silently erases all other Chromium flags
leads.consequence: When the existing flags file is a regular file but is unreadable (e.g. chmod 000), grep exits 2; || true swallows the failure and mv installs the empty temporary file over the old config. The command returns success after writing only two OAuth switches; custom flags and the shipped Wayland/extensions flags are lost. Subsequent runs cannot recover them. Fail on grep errors, preserve the previous file and write only after a successful read.

leads.summary: Fresh installs permanently stamp the floor migration done without checking Chromium
leads.consequence: If a fresh installed system includes Chromium below 152.0.7977.82-1, including an offline or frozen stable build, both /etc/skel and --first-install mark every migration (including this one) complete without running it. The security helper is not on the fresh-install path, and omarchy-migrate later skips it; when repos are too old, the user never even gets the pending floor warning. Later normal -Syu can still repair the browser once repos offer a new build, but the security-floor migration itself never retries. Add the floor check to fresh install/first-run or leave this marker pending when installed Chromium is old.
leads.triage: dropped: stated in the prior public review; fresh installs from stable get the floor build via packages

leads.summary: Chromium Account menu cannot apply any credential rotation once first configured
leads.consequence: After the first successful install, chromium-flags.conf has oauth2-client-id, so the unchanged Chromium Account menu row's disabled guard succeeds; the UI greys it out and removes it from search. A user updating a drop-in cannot rerun from the menu to realize the new credentials, even though repeat invocation is the newly supported rotation path. Direct CLI invocation still works. Make the menu entry selectable for reconfiguration.
leads.triage: dropped: pre-existing and already noted in prior public review; CLI rotation works

leads.summary: The missing-file recovery hint loops for XDG_CONFIG_HOME users
leads.consequence: With XDG_CONFIG_HOME set outside ~/.config and its flags file absent, the new command tells the user to run omarchy-refresh-chromium. That refresh and omarchy-refresh-config only create HOME/.config/chromium-flags.conf, whereas both the new installer and the Arch Chromium launcher read XDG_CONFIG_HOME/chromium-flags.conf. Refresh returns success; retry fails with the same hint, and Chromium sees no new flags. Either refresh the actual XDG path or give a working recovery command.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (F3 edge, negligible: Omarchy does not set XDG_CONFIG_HOME); not published

leads.summary: Explicit missing OAuth env override silently installs packaged credentials
leads.consequence: When OMARCHY_CHROMIUM_OAUTH_ENV is set to a misspelled/deleted file, the for loop ignores the explicit override and sources the packaged fallback, then reports success. An administrator trying to rotate/revoke the packaged pair can instead silently restore that pair; next runs do the same. Distinguish an absent explicit override from the optional drop-ins and error on the former.
leads.triage: factual; coordinator verified installer lines 14-24; Opus C1 a run confirmed; published as maintainer note N5

leads.summary: A failed local pacman database query is misclassified as Chromium not installed
leads.consequence: Any non-zero pacman -Q chromium (including a query/database error rather than actual absence) is swallowed by the migration's if ! guard. It exits 0 and omarchy-migrate writes a permanent done marker without a version check; the helper itself also returns 0 on that error. Update continues without warning. Require positive proof Chromium is absent, or fail to leave migration pending on a query failure.
leads.triage: dropped: low-value edge, not confirmed as reachable in practice

leads.summary: OAuth installer breaks symlinked Chromium flags configs
leads.consequence: A user keeping ~/.config/chromium-flags.conf as a dotfile-manager symlink sees the symlink replaced by an independent 0600 file on the first run. Chromium reads the new file, but the original source is never updated, and future edits to the managed target stop affecting the browser. Repeated runs never restore the link. Update the link target safely or refuse/recover with explicit instructions.

leads.summary: Old OAuth flags inside a multi-switch line survive credential rotation
leads.consequence: The Arch chromium-launcher parses every flag on a line, including an inline --oauth2-client-secret=old-secret, but grep deletes only lines beginning exactly with --oauth2-client-. If the existing flags contain an OAuth switch after another flag or indentation, the old credentials remain on disk after rotation, even though Chromium normally uses the newer switch appended later. The pair is not fully removed as claimed; tests only cover one-switch-per-line. Remove switch tokens according to the launcher's parser, or reject/report unsupported layouts.
leads.triage: dropped: unusual config shape; Chromium still uses the later switch

leads.summary: Open #11907 has an incompatible edit and opposite OAuth lifecycle
leads.consequence: Open omacom/omarchy#11907 diverges from this head, edits the same installer, removes OAuth switches via an added migration, removes refresh's re-add path and changes the UI/docs to prefer Chrome. This PR instead reinstalls the switches from packaged/user OAuth env. Applying #11907's diff on top of this head rejects the installer hunk; a three-way merge has conflict markers. If both features are wanted, reconcile the intended Chromium sign-in behavior, menu, refresh and migrations rather than merging either silently over the other.
leads.triage: factual; coordinator verified #11907 body and installer patch via gh; Opus merge-tree conflict in self-check; published as N4

leads.summary: Security-floor test never exercises the successful upgrade path
leads.consequence: The only dynamic case stubs a repo below the floor, which exits before sudo pacman -S; a plausible regression replacing the upgrade operation with a no-op still passes the entire new test. Add a case with current below floor and available above it, stub sudo/pacman so the installed version changes, and assert both the transaction and post-upgrade floor check. This is a test gap, not a second claim that upgrading currently fails.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (M3 survived); not published separately

limits: Source-based Arch Chromium packaging and launcher v8 plus Chromium 152.0.7977.82 sources checked; no live browser desktop session, actual package operation or network request was run. Open #11907 has a real conflict; other broad search results were screened for path overlap, not every GitHub-wide text-search hit's full diff and merged test run.

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Outcome:** Follow-up on the [earlier review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12244#issuecomment-5835446626), checked at `d5a8885` after the [author's reply](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12244#issuecomment-5841759633). All six earlier findings are resolved, and the suggested test improvement was adopted. The new flags-file rewrite adds one small regression (symlinked or unreadable `chromium-flags.conf`), and the `pacman -Si` parse depends on the locale. Three notes for maintainers follow: what the security-floor helper now does in practice, an open PR that takes the opposite OAuth approach, and a silently skipped override path.

**Verified:**

| Earlier finding | Status at `d5a8885` |
|---|---|
| Security-floor migration marks itself done without upgrading | **Resolved.** The helper exits 1 while Chromium stays below the floor, so `1789400400.sh` stays pending and runs again on the next update. Once the repos offer `152.0.7977.82-1`, the next update brings Chromium to the floor and the migration completes (runs of the real `omarchy-migrate` with `pacman`, `vercmp` and `sudo` stubbed). |
| Security test only greps strings | **Resolved.** The test now runs the helper with stubbed `pacman`, `vercmp` and `sudo`. The inverted-comparison mutant from the earlier review now fails it. |
| Switching OAuth credentials back does not take effect | **Resolved.** Default → override → override removed now leaves the default pair effective, with one pair in the file and other flags kept. The same sequence on the earlier head still leaves the override active. |
| Missing-flags-file hint loops | **Resolved.** `omarchy-refresh-chromium` creates the file, and the re-run then succeeds. |
| `chmod 600` comment overstates | **Resolved.** The comment now says the packaged default credentials stay world-readable. |
| Migration mode, missing `requires-sudo` marker | **Resolved.** The migration is `100644` (a test now checks it), and the helper declares `# omarchy:requires-sudo=true`. |

Of the earlier Verified points, the OAuth resolution order, the unchanged-credentials re-run and mode 600 still hold. Both tests still pass on the head and fail against the base scripts. The `pacman -U <URL>` signature point no longer applies, because the helper now installs with `pacman -S` from the configured repos.

### OAuth rewrite replaces a symlinked flags file and empties an unreadable one

The installer now rewrites the file with `grep -Ev … >"$tmp" || true; mv "$tmp" "$CONF"`:

```text
~/.config/chromium-flags.conf is a symlink into a dotfiles repo
  earlier head   append writes through the link   dotfiles copy updated
  d5a8885        mv replaces the link             regular file; dotfiles copy unchanged

chromium-flags.conf unreadable (mode 000, sandbox edge case)
  earlier head   exits 1, file untouched
  d5a8885        grep fails, "|| true" hides it   file now holds only the 2 OAuth lines; exit 0
```

**Impact:** Users who manage `chromium-flags.conf` as a dotfile symlink lose the link, and later edits to the dotfiles copy stop applying. In the unreadable case every other Chromium flag is dropped. Only a grep permission error is printed, and the script still reports success.

**Suggested change:** Edit in place, as other Omarchy scripts do for user config (for example `bin/omarchy-font-set`):

```bash
sed -i --follow-symlinks -E '/^--oauth2-client-(id|secret)=/d' "$CONF"
```

This keeps the link, fails under `set -e` on an unreadable file, and still matches the test's `oauth2-client-(id|secret)` grep.

**Optional test improvement:** The new re-run test starts from a file that holds only OAuth lines, so a rewrite that dropped every other flag still passes. Seeding one unrelated flag (for example `--ozone-platform=wayland`) and asserting it survives would catch that.

### `pacman -Si` version parse depends on the locale

Helper line 27 matches the English `Version` label, but pacman translates that label (`_("Version")`). It differs in Spanish ("Versión"), Russian, Chinese, Japanese, Brazilian Portuguese, Italian and Polish, and stays "Version" in German and French. In a stubbed run with Spanish labels and a floor build available, the helper exits 1 with "no chromium package is available in the configured repos" and does not upgrade. Separately, when no repo has `chromium`, `pacman -Si` exits non-zero and `set -euo pipefail` aborts the script at that assignment, so the "no package available" message never prints.

**Impact:** With an `IgnorePkg` hold on chromium, `pacman -Syu` skips Chromium while the repos already offer the floor build. In a translated locale the helper then exits 1 without upgrading (stubbed run), while with the English label it upgrades. Otherwise only the explanation is affected: inside `omarchy update` this path is reached only when the repos are already below the floor, so the exit status is 1 either way. The message is wrong in a translated locale and missing when the package is absent.

**Suggested change:** Use `LC_ALL=C pacman -Si chromium 2>/dev/null | awk … || true`, matching `LC_ALL=C pacman -Qi` in `bin/omarchy-upgrade-to-quattro`.

### Notes for maintainers

- **What the security-floor half now does:** `omarchy update` runs `pacman -Syu` before migrations, and the helper installs from that same sync database. So it can no longer lift Chromium above what `-Syu` just installed. As of 2026-09-28 the stable mirror's `extra.db` lists `chromium 152.0.7977.82-1`, exactly the floor, so on standard installs the migration completes as a no-op. It still has two effects of its own:
  - **Blocked updates:** when the configured repos lack the floor build (for example a pinned or custom mirror), the migration exits 1. `omarchy-migrate` then stops the queue and `omarchy update` fails, which a stubbed run of the head `omarchy-update` confirmed. Later migrations wait behind it. `agents/skills/migrations.md` endorses this pattern, but here the blocking condition is the mirror's contents, which the migration cannot repair.
  - **IgnorePkg holds:** under an `IgnorePkg` hold on chromium, pacman 7.1's source answers the ignore prompt for an explicit `-S` target with its default "yes" under `--noconfirm`, so the hold is overridden (source-only, not executed).

  Whether the helper is still wanted is a maintainer decision. #10732 was closed as a duplicate of #9064, which is still open.
- **Related open PR:** #11907 rewrites the same `omarchy-install-chromium-google-account` in the opposite direction. It strips the `--oauth2-client-*` flags, stops `omarchy-refresh-chromium` from re-adding them and points Google sign-in at Chrome, citing SIGTRAP crashes on Chromium 136+ (#2225). The two cannot both land as written.
- **Explicit override path:** when `OMARCHY_CHROMIUM_OAUTH_ENV` names a file that does not exist, `load_oauth_env` skips it silently. It falls through to the user, `/etc` and packaged files and reports success, so a mistyped override goes unnoticed.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Source review of the change since `a4a898f` and the affected update, migration and flags-file code at `d5a8885`, plus pacman 7.1 source, Arch `chromium` packaging, `chromium-launcher` v8 and Chromium 152 switch parsing. The installer scenarios, both tests, mutation checks and the helper, migration runner and update pipeline (its other steps stubbed) were run in a sandbox with `pacman`, `vercmp` (a Python port, not the real binary), `sudo`, `curl` and `uname` stubbed. No real package transaction, sudo or live update was run. Mirror state comes from read-only fetches of public mirror files on 2026-09-28. The IgnorePkg and translated-label behavior is from pacman source; the translated `Version` label in stubbed output was taken from pacman's translation files. aarch64 was not assessed.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.

**Opt out:** To stop receiving these reviews, reply to this comment saying so.
